comments.author: Priya Sharma
comments.body: Got another report this morning—digest for workspace w_9182 listed the same comment twice around the Pacific midnight cutover. Whatever we thought was fixed last sprint is still happening on production.

content.text: Got another report this morning—digest for workspace w_9182 listed the same comment twice around the Pacific midnight cutover. Whatever we thought was fixed last sprint is still happening on production.

Daily digest emails assembled after 00:00 UTC sometimes list the same card activity twice when the underlying event timestamp sits within a few minutes of the day boundary. A workspace that ran a digest at 00:07 UTC saw three assignment changes from 23:58–00:02 appear once under “Yesterday” and again under “Today”.

Expected behavior is that each event_id contributes to exactly one digest window. The window should close on the exclusive upper bound of the previous calendar day in the workspace timezone, not on the worker’s clock alone.

What we observe is double inclusion whenever the digest job’s dayKey is derived from UTC while event buckets are still keyed with America/Los_Angeles offsets. The likely root cause is that DigestAggregator.hashBucket(workspaceId, dayKey) reuses the UTC day string even after the timezone shift was applied to the query filter, so events near midnight land in two buckets before dedupe runs.
Recipients on plans with digests enabled get noisy mail and start marking Nimbus as spam. Support has three open threads from last week referencing this pattern.
